claim_set.claim_text: Every AI-generated public-sector decision, determination, or output that moves toward a consequential action MUST map to a recorded named-authority decision — the agent, the output artefact, the intended consequential action, and the named official under whose authority it proceeds. Outputs lacking a recorded authority decision are refused at the action-admissibility gate.

Before an AI-generated output proceeds to a consequential action it MUST carry a recorded due-diligence result — personnel-eligibility / US-persons screen (FedRAMP PS-3/PS-7) where applicable, a lawful-basis determination (UK GDPR Art.6 public-task; NIS2 governance; ISO/IEC 42001), and a FedRAMP continuous-monitoring / control-status screen (CA-7; open POA&M; SI-2). An unscreened, ineligible-personnel, unlawful-basis, or ConMon-deficient output is refused.

Every AI-generated output that proceeds toward a consequential action MUST emit a signed, replay-derivable provenance pin — produced with FIPS 140-validated cryptographic modules (FedRAMP SC-13) inside a FedRAMP boundary — binding the generating model and version, the inputs and pinned source data, the lawful-basis and ConMon status, the due-diligence result relied on, and the named-authority outcome — audit-grade, FedRAMP-aligned data-integrity provenance verifiable offline.

An AI-generated output MUST remain advisory and MUST NOT drive a consequential action until a named human reviewer — the responsible caseworker, system owner, or authorising official — records sign-off. The irreversible authorising-official-facing assertion (a ConMon / POA&M submission relied on for the ATO) additionally requires §36 two-person sign-off (the preparing system owner AND an approving authorising official). Unreviewed AI-driven consequential actions are refused and routed dual-channel.

KYE governs WHETHER an AI-generated public-sector output may proceed to a consequential action and PROVES the basis. KYE does not replace the FedRAMP / ATO authorisation of the system, make the policy decision, run the case-management engine, or judge whether the determination is substantively correct.
